name: Diego Simeone
scopeNote: Spells counted (user decided): Estudiantes 2006-05-18 to 2007-12-03 (Apertura 2006), River Plate 2007-12-15 to 2008-11-07 (Clausura 2008), Atlético Madrid 2011-12-23 to ongoing. Style called 4-4-2 deep/mid block with zonal screening (Coaches' Voice, Spielverlagerung); later 3-5-2/5-3-2 hybrid from 2020-21. 'Cholismo' is a media/cultural label which Simeone himself distanced from (fifa.com 2015). Evidence for Estudiantes and River is thin (match reports and a retrospective only, no tier A-B tactical coverage found). Atlético change over time: 2012 4-4-1-1 with fast transitions; 2013/14 4-4-2 narrow, wingers inside, full-backs press wide; 2015/16 deep 4-4-2 with a wing-forward variant; 2020-21 3-5-2 with wing-backs; 2023/24 3-5-2 with carrileros; 2024/25 set-piece short-corner work. Dates for spells taken from the user brief, not re-sourced. Source dates are partial where the match day was not found. Excluded spells carry year-only dates because the user brief gave years only.
openQuestions: No tier A-B source found that describes Atlético's own corner defence as zonal, man or mixed; only the Coaches' Voice zonal-marking explainer (open play) and an attacking short-corner study.
Estudiantes 2006-07 and River 2007-08 have no tactical analysis found; shape/pressing for these spells unverified.
Joao Félix relationship is press narrative (El Debate); Simeone's own statements not mined.
The Masterminds Site 2020-21 analysis returned 403; could not be used.
Whether 'partido a partido' is a primary Simeone quote: Público (2014) calls it a 'mantra' without a dated quote.

sources.title: Zonal marking: football tactics explained - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: Diego Simeone has often favoured a low block with Atlético Madrid, with compactness between units and individuals totally key. Using his favoured 4-4-2, the two centre-forwards zonally screen the opposing pivots, with both wide midfielders then narrowing to cover the inside channels (below). The aim here is to force the ball wide, with the entire back four sliding across and the full-backs aggressive in closing down opponents in the wide channels.
sources.note: undated period description; Coaches' Voice speaks of Simeone's favoured 4-4-2 low block, no season given

sources.title: Atlético Madrid under Diego Simeone in 2014 - Spielverlagerung
sources.evidence: Atletico Madrid often play in a 4-4-2 with a deep midfield press. The two strikers work up to the central midfield and the midfield chain is narrower than the defensive line.

sources.title: Atlético Madrid under Diego Simeone in 2014 - Spielverlagerung
sources.evidence: The narrow midfield chain and the dynamic shifting of their other teammates forces the opponent to pass to the sidelines, giving Atlético almost constant control over the center of the pitch.

sources.title: Atlético Madrid under Diego Simeone in 2014 - Spielverlagerung
sources.evidence: Atlético clenched so tight that a pass into the intermediate line space was impossible. There was a clear 4-4-2 and the horizontal lines in the bands seemed to almost be drawn straight across the pitch.

sources.title: Atlético Madrid under Diego Simeone in 2014 - Spielverlagerung
sources.evidence: The wingers set up in the midfield rather than on the wings in order to occupy the half-spaces and provide horizontal compactness. Because of this and the movement of the two strikers, the opponent is lured to the wings, where they are then very aggressively pressed.

sources.title: Atlético Madrid under Diego Simeone in 2014 - Spielverlagerung

sources.title: Atlético Madrid under Diego Simeone in 2014 - Spielverlagerung

That said, I wouldn’t go so far as to talk about ‘Cholismo’, even if my teams do play in a certain way. We don’t just play direct football because they are cliches that are used when a team can’t find a way past us.
Muchas veces uno sale con defensa de cuatro, pero nunca es cuatro, porque el banda de la izquierda o el banda de la derecha termina siendo el quinto
